summary: The agent implemented the configurable collection feature successfully enough to pass all 53 new tests, but introduced a generated-source regression that caused 26 baseline fixture tests to fail.
quick_failure_summary: Existing generated mapper fixtures changed local-variable names in an unconfigured collection-mapping path.

details.reasoning: All hidden feature tests passed, showing that the main implementation is substantial and correct. However, the agent added an unconditional createUniqueVarName call to SetterWrapperForCollectionsAndMapsWithNullCheck. Even when no configured implementation is active, that call consumes variable names and changes generated source such as 'set' to 'set1' and 'set1' to 'set4'. The 26 baseline failures are all exact generated-source fixture mismatches in Issue913SetterMapperForCollectionsTest, directly exercising the modified wrapper/template path. The reference solution avoids modifying that common wrapper and instead routes configured direct assignments through NewInstanceSetterWrapperForCollectionsAndMaps, preserving existing output. Under the required decision tree, passing new tests while failing baseline tests in touched code is a regression.
details.secondary_factors: The agent validated focused and adjacent collection/stream tests, but its final verify commands used -DskipTests, so it did not run the full baseline suite that would have exposed the fixture regression. The full Maven run also reported four additional failures outside the grader's baseline node set, but the structured grading result independently establishes the 26 baseline regressions.

problem_assessment.notes: The prompt clearly specifies resource loading, duplicate validation, later-round resolution, generic and constructor constraints, capacity construction, direct properties, streams, and factory precedence. The 53 new tests comprehensively and deterministically cover those requirements. Preserving existing generated output is a normal repository regression constraint, and the reference solution demonstrates a feasible implementation that passes without perturbing the common wrapper's variable allocation.

evidence: The structured new-test report records 53 tests with 0 failures and 0 errors, so the verifier exercised the feature successfully.

The structured baseline report records 3641 tests with 26 failures and 0 errors; every graded failure is an exact fixture mismatch in Issue913SetterMapperForCollectionsTest showing renamed local variables.
The failing generated code comes from SetterWrapperForCollectionsAndMapsWithNullCheck, which the agent modified to call createUniqueVarName unconditionally.

The trajectory shows successful compilation, focused tests on both compilers, and successful verify runs; there are no observed missing dependencies, permissions errors, runtime crashes, API failures, or service failures.

Although the post-agent harness logged a recoverable three-way test.patch merge failure, it reset the affected files, completed both runs, and all 53 new tests passed, so that event did not cause the graded failure.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the baseline failure is caused by an avoidable generated-source naming regression in agent-modified code.
